subject: Pulse Retail Q2 headroom request — tiered overrun settlement
messages:
From: Emma Zhang <emma@pulse-retail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q2 promo — short-term headroom needed

Hi Irene,

We're ramping a nationwide spring promo on April 12 and our forecast shows a ~3x spike in inference volume for a 72-hour window (peak around Apr 12-14). Currently we have the Standard tier with a 5k RPS equivalent quota and a 1MB/minute rate limit — that will bottleneck the campaign.

Can Redwood support a short-term quota uplift and rate-limit bump for that window? We're open to: a) a 72-hour burst with overrun settlement, b) a short committed uplift for 7 days, or c) pre-purchased burst credits. Please include pricing that reflects blended overrun rates (we're sensitive to cost) and any quick-approval path so we can confirm before our creative freeze on 2028-03-23.

Attaching a snapshot of our expected usage profile.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Zhang
Head of Platform
Pulse Retail
(Attachment: usage-snapshot.csv)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhang <emma@pulse-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 promo — short-term headroom needed

Hi Emma — thanks for the details and the timeline. We can absolutely support a safe path for the April window; below are two pragmatic options with estimated economics so your procurement team can pick a path quickly.

Option A — 72-hour burst (recommended for minimal ops):
- Temporary quota bump to 3x baseline for 72 hours (Apr 12 00:00 UTC — Apr 15 00:00 UTC).
- Overrun settlement: blended overage rate equal to 1.15x list per-token rate, with a 5% promo discount if Pulse agrees to a 3-month minimum committed spend (invoice credit applied).
- No long-term contract change; automatic revert after window.

Option B — 7-day short commit:
- 7-day uplift at negotiated flat uplift rate; lower per-token overage (1.05x list) but requires a short-term commit and a small one-time setup fee.

Next steps (fast path):
1) We can issue a short SOW for Option A today (DocuSign).
2) Procurement sign-off or PO — we can accept standard Pulse PO.
3) Provide final contact for procurement and a billing contact.

I attached a draft SOW that captures the 72-hour burst terms and the blended overrun math. Happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through numbers.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: PRP_Q2_Uplift_SOW.pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Q2 promo — short-term headroom needed (internal)

Ben / Grace — quick internal: Emma's asking for the 72-hour spike. Proposed commercial is 1.15x list blended overrun with a 5% promo discount if they take a 3-month minimum.

Questions for pricing:
- Can we push a margin floor such that blended overrun >= 0.9x our billable baseline?
- If procurement pushes back, are we comfortable with a small setup fee to preserve margin?

I suggest we pre-approve the SOW for Option A and present Option B as an alternative if procurement wants a lower per-token. I'll include the SOW in the outbound but want pricing approval before DocuSign goes live.

On it to expedite — Irene

Thanks, Irene — Option A looks like the fastest path for us. Procurement is looped (procurement@pulse-retail.com) and will need a DocuSign SOW and the PO-friendly billing language. Two quick clarifications before we sign:
1) If we hit a sustained 6x peak for a short period during the 72 hours, does the blended overrun cap at any dollar threshold?
2) Will the temporary rate-limit bump include burst tokens in the KV cache eviction policy (we need consistent latency for auth calls)?

If those look fine we'll proceed with DocuSign. When you send the SOW can you also include the HubSpot record id so our procurement team references the right account.

— Emma

Emma / procurement team — thank you. Answers below and DocuSign link included.

1) Peak cap: We will cap blended overrun liability at a pre-agreed dollar ceiling equal to 2x the estimated burst charge (calculated from your provided snapshot) unless Pulse explicitly signs a higher cap. That protects both sides and keeps approvals simple.
2) KV/cache behavior & latency: The temporary rate-limit bump will include the burst tokens in the same cache/eviction policy; we've validated expected latency ranges with infra and will allocate additional padding to maintain tail latency SLAs during the window.

HubSpot record: HS-89621
DocuSign SOW: https://docusign.example.com/EX-12345

If procurement can sign by 2028-03-21 we will schedule the uplift and routing changes and confirm the exact UTC windows. Once signed we'll send a confirmation email with the effective timestamps and a short runbook for your infra team.

Thanks — looking forward to supporting the campaign.

— Irene
